svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: iOS · Gallery · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/GalleryView.swift (compact branch — hSizeClass .compact, and the iPhone-portrait header form chosen by GalleryView.isPhonePortrait: UIDevice idiom .phone AND verticalSizeClass .regular) + App/GallerySidebar.swift (the Library sheet the ▤ button raises: kind filter rows, present tags, Collections) + App/GalleryGridContent.swift (standardGrid) + App/GalleryTile.swift + App/GalleryPreviewPanel.swift (the sheet a single tap raises on compact). Redrawn 2026-09-08, app-first: Steven's iPhone screenshot showed the Mac header reused verbatim — one HStack of eight children about 691pt wide on a 361pt content column, nothing collapsing — so SwiftUI crushed the 20pt "Gallery" title to zero width (it wrapped one glyph per line, which was the ~180pt blank band above the controls), the search field clipped at the leading edge, the Timeline toggle fell off the trailing edge, and the whole VStack — grid included — laid out ~600pt wide and centred, so tiles spilled off both sides. Reproduced on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator before the change. HEADER, iPhone portrait only: the tab's large title, 34pt bold, baseline 106 and 20pt in — the same rhythm as projects.portrait.svg and every other tab here — with three controls opposite it, centred 6pt above the baseline (y 100) exactly as the Projects sharing chip is (the same alignmentGuide), trailing inset 16, 8pt apart: ▤ Library (sidebar.left, 32×32 at radius 7 on primary@5%, glyph 16pt medium — secondary here, LL.accent once the kind filter or a tag is narrowing the library, since showSidebar is a Mac pane state and reading it lit the button permanently on a phone) · the sort capsule and direction button unchanged from the Mac (Capture ˅ 13pt medium on a 28pt capsule at primary@6%, the 28pt triangle 4pt after it; Capture · Added · Edit · Size) · Timeline as a glyph (calendar, the library button's twin, LL.accent while timeline mode is on). NO SEARCH FIELD on an upright iPhone, by decision (Steven, 2026-09-08 — "kill the search input to clear things up, iPhone portrait only"): the row is filter · order · mode, and a 190pt field cost the whole header. NO ZOOM SLIDER either: the grid takes a pinch over the same 2–6 columns through the same gallery.columnCount key. Everything else — iPad, Mac, iPhone landscape — keeps the full single row (macOS/gallery.svg), where the search field now yields down to 120pt before anything else gives; that is what keeps an SE's 635pt landscape row from overflowing the way portrait did. Header band: top padding 15, title frame 74–115, bottom padding 10, hairline Divider at 125.5. GRID (GalleryGridContent.standardGrid): ScrollView, .padding(.horizontal, 14) and .padding(.vertical, 14), LazyVGrid of columnCount flexible columns at spacing 12 — at the drawn columnCount of 3 that is a 365pt content width and 113.67×85.25pt tiles, drawn 4:3 by GalleryTile's .aspectRatio(4/3, contentMode: .fit) at cornerRadius 8; column origins 14 / 139.67 / 265.33, row pitch 97.25 from y 140. TILE: a MediaBadge naming the shoot type pinned bottom-leading with 6pt padding (black@50%, white 11.5pt semibold, 24pt tall) and an amber "N clips" badge top-trailing with the same padding, only where model.blends(for:).count ≥ 2 (one drawn, row 2). Single tap selects and raises GalleryPreviewPanel as a sheet; long-press raises the context menu (Open · New blended clip · Edit · Delete…), not drawn. The last rows scroll under the floating tab bar; the ScrollView appends an 82pt spacer for it. STATES NOT DRAWN: the Library sheet (a NavigationStack titled "Library" with Done), the preview sheet, timeline mode (macOS/gallery.timeline.svg draws the grouping), the empty state ("No projects" over "Adjust the filter or search to see your library." — still says search on a phone that no longer has one, noted in INDEX.md), the "Couldn't delete" alert. HOOKS: LL_TAB=gallery; sort, direction, column count and timeline mode are @AppStorage (gallery.sortKey / gallery.sortAscending / gallery.columnCount / gallery.timelineMode), seeded before launch. Verified against the iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.1) on 2026-09-08; device sign-off owed. **2026-09-15 — the SYNC PILL takes the Timeline glyph's seat** (Steven: the Projects header's icon in the Gallery too; on the phone in portrait in the Timeline button's place, the Timeline button retired from that row). The pill is the same ProjectSharingChip (green serving / red not / amber failed) over the model's one ProjectTransferServer — moved from ProjectsView's @StateObject to AppModel so the two headers show one state — and opens the same "Project Syncing" sheet (projects.sharing.portrait.svg: PicPlace over nearby devices). The Timeline switch lives in the ▤ Library sheet now (gallery.library-sheet.portrait.svg, a VIEW section on top), because the mode is remembered and a phone must be able to leave it. iPad, Mac and iPhone landscape keep the Timeline button in the full row and draw the pill to its right; that row is now a ViewThatFits — the full row where it fits, else a tighter one with no zoom slider and Timeline as its glyph (an iPad held upright with the sidebar open, an SE in landscape). A deliberate pull on the grid — the standard grid's and the timeline's scroll views, not the month rail — is "Check PicPlace now" (`.refreshable`); the check's arrivals reach this grid and the Projects list through the index. Verified on the iPhone 16 Pro simulator (iOS 18.6), signed out, and an iPad Pro 11 simulator for the tight row, 2026-09-15.
svg.text: mirrors App/GalleryView.swift compactHeader — large title · ▤ Library · sort · sync pill · 3-column 4:3 GalleryGridContent
